objective: Show that hub-free networks of three-place relations, where every shared distinction joins exactly two copies, are pants decompositions of compact orientable surfaces with Euler characteristic minus the number of copies and one boundary circle per open distinction, while two-place relations glue only into lines and loops. Prove that for the parity knots the glued result depends only on the boundary and the total charge, with two to the genus witness assignments per allowed boundary state. Census every Boolean three-place relation on small surfaces and certify that every other knot either forgets (frozen) or depends on more than the surface.
status: Proved by SURFACE-GLUING-20261024-001A-P001 (V1 prose proof, standard-library check passed). Hub-free networks of three-place relations are pants decompositions of compact orientable surfaces (two-place relations give only paths and cycles). A symmetric three-place relation glues topologically exactly when two glued copies are symmetric in their four legs. Exactly four of the 34 knots glue topologically with witness counts: the two parity knots (one hidden bit per handle) and the two no-lone-value knots (spheres only; closed genus-g counts tr H^(g-1) with H = [[3,1],[1,2]], eigenvalue ratio the golden ratio squared). The two frozen knots forget once glued; not-all-equal and the 27 asymmetric knots see more than the surface.
title: Native gluing builds surfaces, and only parity sees just the surface
